assisted_eq.card_desc: EQ that sets itself from the track
assisted_eq.keywords: assisted eq equalizer learn auto automatic smart assistant tone match mud boxy harsh dull warm bright radio podcast lo-fi vocal drums bass mix
slider_desc: Press On and play the track: it listens for 15 s of signal (or until you turn it Off, after at least 0.5 s), then stores what it heard and returns to Off.
What is playing: Vocal, Drums, Bass, Instrument or Mix. Each has its own healthy balance that Learn corrects toward.
The sound you want: Natural (only corrects), Warm, Bright, Punchy, Radio, Podcast or Lo-Fi.
How much of the learned correction and target is applied, 0-150%.
Your own shelf at 100 Hz on top.
Your own bell at 1 kHz on top.
Your own shelf at 10 kHz on top.
Level after the EQ, on top of the automatic level match.
Hidden: whether Learn has run. Saved with the project.
Hidden: the learned level of the lows (60-120 Hz) against the reference, in dB.
Hidden: the learned level of the mud region (200-500 Hz) against the reference, in dB.
Hidden: the frequency where the mud peaks.
Hidden: the learned level of the honk region (800 Hz-1.6 kHz) against the reference, in dB.
Hidden: the learned level of the presence region (2-5 kHz) against the reference, in dB.
Hidden: the learned level of the air region (8-16 kHz) against the reference, in dB.
Hidden: the lowest band with real content; the learned high-pass sits below it.
uses: A first EQ on a vocal without knowing where to cut
Taking the mud out of a recording with one button
Radio, podcast or phone sound on a voice
A quick, safe tone balance on a bus or a mix
assisted_eq.properties: Learn: 29 third-octave band-passes in 50 ms windows (only windows above -60 dBFS count), measured against a -4.5 dB/oct reference levelled at 500 Hz-4 kHz, grouped into low, mud, honk, presence and air. Rules (tools/assisted_targets.json): 60% of each deviation from the source's healthy balance beyond 1.5 dB is corrected (-6 to +4 dB, mud only cut), plus the target's flavour, times Amount. EQ: high-pass (learned and target), low shelf 100 Hz, mud bell, honk bell 1 kHz, presence bell 3 kHz, air shelf 10 kHz, target low-pass (RBJ biquads) → automatic level match → Output. No AI: fixed rules, the same result every time. Zero latency.

assisted_comp.card_desc: Compressor that sets itself from the track
assisted_comp.keywords: assisted compressor comp dynamics learn auto automatic smart assistant threshold attack release loudness lufs podcast radio punchy vocal drums bass bus
slider_desc: Press On and play the track: it listens for 15 s of signal (or until you turn it Off, after at least 0.5 s), then stores what it heard and returns to Off.
What is playing: Vocal, Drums, Bass, Instrument or Mix. Each has its own ratio.
The sound you want: Natural, Warm, Bright, Punchy, Radio, Podcast (also brings the loudness to -16 LUFS) or Lo-Fi.
How much of the target's gain reduction is applied, 0-150%.
More (+) or less (-) compression than the target: moves the threshold down or up.
Faster (+) or slower (-): +1 halves attack and release, -1 doubles them.
Blend between the dry and the compressed signal (parallel compression).
Level after compression and makeup, on top of the automatic loudness of Podcast.
Hidden: whether Learn has run. Saved with the project.
Hidden: the learned level of the loud parts (90th percentile of the 50 ms levels).
Hidden: the learned median level.
Hidden: the learned crest factor (peak over RMS).
Hidden: the learned mean time between onsets (0 = none found).
Hidden: the learned integrated loudness (BS.1770).
uses: A first compressor on a vocal without knowing the settings
A podcast voice at -16 LUFS with one button
Drum bus punch or parallel crush
Gentle glue on a bus or a mix
assisted_comp.properties: Learn: level histogram of 50 ms windows (0.1 dB bins, only windows above -60 dBFS count), mean crest factor, onset intervals (a 5 ms envelope jumping 6 dB over a 100 ms one) and BS.1770 integrated loudness. Rules (tools/assisted_targets.json): the target's reduction on the loud parts times Amount sets the threshold; ratio per source plus a target step (1.5:1-10:1); attack 5-25 ms by crest factor times the target's factor; release 60% of the onset interval (50-500 ms); makeup gives back half the reduction; Podcast moves Output to -16 LUFS. Compressor: stereo-linked peak detector → 6 dB soft knee → attack/release smoothing → makeup → Mix → Output. No AI: fixed rules, the same result every time. Zero latency.
